subclaim.statement: The core returns the specified flow-policy verdicts and exact finite taint closure, including hidden-policy promotion seeds.

subclaim.assumptions: Trusted host supplies normalized observations; adapter, isolated worker, Dafny, compiler and runtime remain trusted.
subclaim.input_model: Normalized call observations include five required textual citations: scope, argument hash, source capsule, instruction/data split and cold replay. Write and external mutation also require approval, ledger and rollback text.
subclaim.limits: Normalization, declared-tool membership and receipt rendering are host responsibilities; nonempty text does not authenticate approvals, resolve references or validate a cryptographic hash.
subclaim.statement: Each of ten ordered fault flags matches its rule; a three-call batch passes exactly with all rows accepted, one qualifying write and one untrusted-result row.

subclaim.assumptions: The host supplies normalized string and timing observations. The adapter, isolated worker, Dafny, Boogie, Z3, compiler and Python runtime remain trusted.
subclaim.input_model: Finite normalized expected and selected ID sequences, timeout/error/scent/forbidden flags, and signed integer wall time and budget. Missing expected artifacts are derived from the matching counts.
subclaim.limits: Host sorting, observed labels, ratios and rounding are trusted; route quality is not proved.
subclaim.statement: Counts equal the cardinalities of matching expected and selected positions in their separate units. Decisions follow timeout/error/missing/scent/forbidden priority; latency is exactly timeout, within budget or over budget from the integer observations.

subclaim.assumptions: Trusted host supplies normalized observations; adapter, isolated worker, Dafny, compiler and runtime remain trusted.
subclaim.input_model: Finite exact normalized path IDs and supplied live, unknown or stale claim observations; priority is live then unknown then stale.
subclaim.limits: The host must supply truthful freshness and identity; path overlap, real locks and concurrency safety are not proved.
subclaim.statement: Every generated path with a matching live claim is protected regardless of claim order; selection chooses the earliest match at the highest freshness priority.

subclaim.assumptions: Trusted host supplies normalized observations; adapter, isolated worker, Dafny, compiler and runtime remain trusted.
subclaim.input_model: Finite equal-length nonnegative token-count vectors and candidate eligibility, strategy and ID-rank observations.
subclaim.limits: Host tokenization, metadata, split and strategy checks are trusted; ranking usefulness is not proved.
subclaim.statement: Eligible candidate occurrences are scored by token-count overlap plus strategy bonus and sorted by score, ID rank and original position.

subclaim.assumptions: Trusted host supplies normalized observations; adapter, isolated worker, Dafny, compiler and runtime remain trusted.
subclaim.input_model: Four normalized risk, action, capability and source-trust strings.
subclaim.limits: Host normalization is trusted; the proof does not establish real sandbox containment or the authenticity of action records.
subclaim.statement: Six recognized action shapes receive their exact verdict and rule; all other normalized shapes fail closed.

subclaim.assumptions: Trusted host supplies normalized observations; adapter, isolated worker, Dafny, compiler and runtime remain trusted.
subclaim.input_model: Ordered finite preferences and candidate IDs with known, available and allowed observations.
subclaim.limits: Host inputs and availability observations are trusted; selection does not prove a tactic solves the goal.
subclaim.statement: Select the first preferred ID with an eligible candidate, otherwise the first eligible candidate, or report none.

subclaim.assumptions: Trusted host supplies normalized observations; adapter, isolated worker, Dafny, compiler and runtime remain trusted.
subclaim.input_model: Finite normalized steps; positive denominator and numerator, numerator ≤ 10×denominator; at least five steps, four distinct commands and four distinct evidence refs, with each step carrying a command, inspection ref and evidence ref.
subclaim.limits: Observed numeric conversion and host reference locality are trusted; the theorem does not establish elapsed time, file existence or command execution.
subclaim.statement: A normalized walkthrough is accepted exactly when its positive rational budget is at most ten minutes and all step and distinct-reference floors hold.
